newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania pledges sale of State Commercial Bank.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania pledges sale of State Commercial Bank.

text.p: Lithuanian Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta on Friday said the state-owned Lithuanian State Commercial Bank would be sold in 1997.
The bank is on the list of state-owned banks the government has pledged to privatise under World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF) programmes.
"We expect that the privatision of the State Commercial Bank will be over before the end of the year," Shemeta told a news conference.
He did not give a value for the bank, which is a leading bank but has suffered serious liquidity problems.
Shemeta said that next week the finance ministry would send invitations to investment banks to draw up a privatisation programme for the State Commercial Bank.
Shemeta said the deadline for replies was the end of March and a winner would be announced by mid-May.
A privatisation deal is expected to be signed in the middle of August, Shemeta added. The whole of the state's 100 percent of the State Commercial Bank shares would be sold, he said.
"We are looking for a strategic investor, an investor who can not only buy but also provide further essential investments in its development and management," Shemeta said.
